title: Find Subtree Sizes After Changes
summary: Given a tree rooted at node 0 with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a character assigned to it, perform the following operation for each node x from 1 to n-1: 1.
statement: Given a tree rooted at node 0 with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a character assigned to it, perform the following operation for each node x from 1 to n-1: 1. Identify the closest ancestor y of node x such that s[x] is equal to s[y]. 2. If such an ancestor y exists, remove the edge between x and its current parent and add an edge between y and x, making y the new parent of x. Return an array where the i-th element represents the size of the subtree rooted at node i in the tree after performing the above operations.
constraints: parent and s describe a rooted tree of up to 100,000 nodes; parent[0] is -1.
Every nonroot node simultaneously moves to its closest original ancestor with the same character, if one exists.
Return all subtree sizes in the final tree.
hints: Simultaneous changes must consult ancestors in the original tree, not parents already changed.
During original-tree DFS, keep a stack of active ancestors for each character.
Assign the closest matching stack top, then aggregate final sizes from descendants toward ancestors.
The active stack exactly represents original ancestors; every new parent remains an ancestor, so reverse DFS order safely accumulates each subtree once.
editorial: The active stack exactly represents original ancestors; every new parent remains an ancestor, so reverse DFS order safely accumulates each subtree once.

tests.explanation: Node 3 moves from parent 1 to same-character ancestor 0; final sizes are 6,3,1,1,1,1.
Nodes 4 and 2 choose closest matching ancestors in the original tree, producing sizes 5,2,1,1,1.
